creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Point at one pane, scroll, and a different pane moves - whichever has the
keyboard. Ghostty scrolls where the pointer is, and so should Muster:
reading one agent's output while typing into another is the ordinary case
in a window of fifteen, and this makes it impossible without first
clicking away from what you were typing in.

**The right view already receives the event; it just does not say who it
is.** AppKit hit-tests `scrollWheel` to the view under the pointer, so
`SurfaceView.scrollWheel` fires on the correct surface. It then calls
`Core.scroll(direction:delta:)`, and `Scroll` in the proto carries a
direction and a delta and nothing else - so the core routes it with
`with_pane("a scroll", ...)`, which resolves to `session::keyboard_pane()`.
The pane identity is discarded one line above where it is needed.

The shape of the fix, which is small:

- `Scroll` gains a pane and a daemon. Both, not just the pane - two
  daemons hand out the same ids, and every other pane-addressed message
  here carries the pair for that reason.
- `SurfaceView` fills them from the chrome it belongs to. The pattern
  already exists: a click sends `onFocusRequested` with the pane id, and
  there is a test pinning that it names the right one.
- The handler routes to the named pane instead of the keyboard pane.

**Scrolling must not move the keyboard.** Worth stating because the
tempting implementation is to reuse the focus path, and Ghostty does not
steal focus on scroll either - the whole point is reading one pane while
typing into another. Two edges mean two things here, as they do
everywhere else in this window.

Decide while implementing: what a scroll over a pane with no channel does
(nothing, presumably, and silently rather than as a refusal - the pointer
being somewhere is not a request), and whether the scroll should follow
the pointer across a region boundary mid-gesture or stay with the pane it
started on. macOS momentum scrolling makes the second one visible.
title: 🖱️ Scrolling should move the pane under the mouse, not the focused one
